title: Lease Term Agreement Notice to Vacate and Holdover Schedule
content:
Each Lease Term Agreement program fixes how much written notice a resident gives before the intended move-out date, whether and for how long a notice may be withdrawn, the channels through which written notice is accepted, how the insufficient notice charge is computed and the daily holdover rent multiple.

| Term program | Written notice required (calendar days before the intended move-out date) | Notice may be withdrawn | Withdrawal window (calendar days after the notice is received) | Holdover rent (multiple of the daily contracted rent) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Month-to-Month Agreement | 30 | Yes | 7 | 1.25 |
| Short-Term Lease (3-5 Months) | 30 | Yes | 7 | 1.25 |
| Flexible Lease (6-9 Months) | 45 | Yes | 10 | 1.25 |
| Standard Lease (10-12 Months) | 60 | Yes | 14 | 1.50 |
| Extended Lease (13-15 Months) | 60 | Yes | 14 | 1.50 |
| Long-Term Lease (16-24 Months) | 60 | Yes | 14 | 1.50 |

**Accepted channels (all six programs).** A notice to vacate, an early termination request or a transfer request is accepted through the resident portal or on a signed notice form.

**Basis of the insufficient notice charge (all six programs).** The daily contracted rent: one day of rent is charged per day of notice short.

**Holdover multiple.** A multiple of 1.25 bills each holdover day at one and a quarter times the daily contracted rent; a multiple of 1.50 bills it at one and a half times.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A resident on the Flexible Lease (6-9 Months) program gives written notice through the resident portal; the program asks for 45 calendar days before the intended move-out date and allows withdrawal within 10 calendar days of receipt. A resident on the Long-Term Lease (16-24 Months) program gives 60 days and may withdraw within 14.
